gloss: to encourage; to cheer up; to invigorate

definitions.gloss: to encourage; to cheer up; to invigorate; to hearten
definitions.explanation: To give someone energy, courage, or emotional support. To make someone feel more cheerful or motivated.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}を{元気|げんき}づける。
{落|お}ち{込|こ}んでいる{彼|かれ}を{元気|げんき}づけたい。
examples.english: I want to cheer him up since he's feeling down.

examples.japanese: みんなの{応援|おうえん}が{選手|せんしゅ}たちを{元気|げんき}づけた。

notes:
A compound verb formed from {元気|げんき} (energy, vigor) and the verb-forming suffix づける (to give/impart a quality). Means to give someone {元気|げんき}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}を{元気|げんき}づける: to cheer someone up
- {言葉|ことば}で{元気|げんき}づける: to encourage with words
- {元気|げんき}づけられる: to be cheered up (passive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {励|はげ}ます: to encourage — more general, includes motivating someone to try harder
- {元気|げんき}づける: to cheer up — focuses on restoring emotional energy
- {慰|なぐさ}める: to console — comforting someone who is sad or grieving
- {応援|おうえん}する: to support/cheer for — active support, often in competitive contexts

GRAMMAR:
The intransitive counterpart is {元気|げんき}づく (to become encouraged, to perk up).
